head: Open a table and start reading.
body: Tables grouped by schema in the sidebar. A WHERE box for filters, click a header to sort, scroll for more rows. Foreign keys are marked, and a right-click on one jumps to the row it points at.

head: Nothing is written until you read the SQL.
body: Change cells, insert rows, delete rows. It all stays pending until you press ⌘S and see the exact statements Taula is about to run. Every commit lands in a journal with its inverse, so one click undoes it.

head: A DELETE without a WHERE stops and asks.
body: Taula knows the statements that end badly — UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE, TRUNCATE, DROP TABLE — and makes you confirm before one runs. On a connection you marked production it asks twice and snapshots the table first, so there is something to go back to.

head: Everything is one keystroke away.
body: Tables, columns, snippets, query history, databases, connections, and actions in one fuzzy bar. Type SQL straight into it and get results inline, without opening a tab.

head: Ask in plain language. It runs on your Mac.
body: The assistant inspects your schema, writes the query, and shows you the rows. Anything that would write data comes back as a proposal you approve. The model runs locally with llama.cpp, so nothing leaves the machine and there is no key to paste.

head: Every write is stored with its inverse.
body: Each commit — from the grid, from a script, from a proposal you approved — is journaled next to the SQL that undoes it. Open it with ⌘K, read what actually happened, and put one entry back without going looking for a backup.

head: See how the tables fit together.
body: Every foreign key drawn as an edge. Click a table to focus its relations, double-click to open it. Schema diff and data diff live one menu away when two databases have drifted.
